items.title: Colombo restaurant fined Rs. 100,000 over expired cooking oil bottle
items.author: Editor Z
items.summary: A Colombo restaurant operating company was fined Rs. 100,000 by the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court for violating Consumer Affairs Authority regulations regarding the storage of expired products. The enforcement highlights regulatory compliance requirements for food businesses.

items.title: The Rupee-Dollar Trap: Why Strict PFMA Compliance Won’t Automatically Free Sri Lanka from the IMF in 2027
items.author: LBO
items.summary: Analysts discuss Sri Lanka's economic strategy and options as the IMF Extended Fund Facility approaches its conclusion in March 2027. While the Public Financial Management Act establishes strict fiscal guardrails for the national budget, experts warn that addressing external debt service and reserve adequacy remains critical. The debate focuses on long-term macroeconomic independence and sustainability.

items.title: Sri Lanka’s Lakdhanavi secures USD 75 million contract for 57 MW power plant in India
items.author: Editor A
items.summary: Sri Lankan engineering firm Lakdhanavi has secured a USD 75 million turnkey contract to construct a natural gas-fired power plant in India's Andaman and Nicobar Islands. This marks the company's entry into India's EPC power plant market following an international competitive bidding process. The milestone demonstrates the growing regional footprint of Sri Lankan engineering expertise.

items.author: Editor A
items.summary: Tesla has begun offering selected United States customers the option to purchase its fully autonomous Cybercab for personal use, priced at US$29,990 with a mandatory monthly subscription. The vehicle operates entirely through autonomous driving technology without a steering wheel or pedals.

items.title: It is the government’s aim to make the entrepreneurship one of the driving forces in the national economy – Prime Minister
items.author: Priyan
items.summary: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya stated that the government aims to make entrepreneurship a primary driver of national economic growth and development. Speaking at an awards ceremony, she highlighted budget measures designed to support domestic industries, job creation, and export-oriented businesses. Strengthening the SME sector is viewed as essential for building a resilient economy.

items.title: Bing Chun responds to Rs. 84,000 fine over ice cream standards violations
items.author: Editor A
items.summary: Bing Chun Sri Lanka was fined Rs. 84,000 by the Maligakanda Magistrate’s Court after ice cream samples failed to meet compositional standards. The company clarified that the products were not deemed unsafe for consumption while reviewing its quality processes.

items.title: Sri Lanka’s monthly tourism revenue up 3.5-pct in October 2026
items.author: Shihar Aneez
items.summary: Sri Lanka’s monthly foreign exchange revenue from tourism rose 3.5 percent year-on-year in October 2026 to US$192.7 million, marking the third consecutive month of growth. However, total tourism revenue for the first ten months remained 8.3 percent lower compared to the same period last year.

items.title: Lanka plans more subsidized credit amid high inflation target
items.author: Thilina Walpola
items.summary: The government has allocated substantial funds in the upcoming budget for interest subsidies and refinancing schemes to provide concessionary loans to entrepreneurs. Additional subsidized credit programs are targeted at specific demographics, including migrant workers. These financial support measures aim to boost domestic enterprise development amidst high inflation.

items.title: Sajith accuses Government of betraying election promises with Budget 2027
items.author: Thilina Walpola
items.summary: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa criticized the 2027 national budget during parliamentary debates, claiming it places excessive burdens on the poor and abandons previous welfare promises. He pointed to widening income inequality and rising living costs as key economic challenges. The critique underscores ongoing political discourse surrounding Sri Lanka's fiscal policies.

items.title: Mayor Balthazaar warns of legal action over AI-generated Colombo flood videos
items.author: Thilina Walpola
items.summary: Colombo Mayor Vraie Cally Balthazaar has warned of legal action against individuals circulating AI-generated videos falsely showing flooding inside a Colombo shopping mall. Fact-checking groups confirmed the viral footage was manipulated using artificial intelligence tools. This highlights growing concerns surrounding misinformation and the misuse of generative AI technologies in Sri Lanka.

items.title: Lanka moves to expand India FTA
items.author: Thilina Walpola
items.summary: Sri Lanka has appointed an official committee to explore expanding its existing Free Trade Agreement with India and is pursuing new trade pacts with other regional partners. The government aims to enhance export competitiveness and diversify its trade base through updated international agreements and EU grant assistance. These steps are part of a broader strategy to boost national exports.

items.title: GovTech to setup Digital Transformation Academy – MTI strategizes
items.author: LBO
items.summary: The Asian Development Bank has retained MTI Consulting to design the strategy and curriculum for Sri Lanka's new Academy for Digital Transformation under GovTech. The academy will build digital capabilities within the public sector workforce to accelerate digital government initiatives and Digital Public Infrastructure. This is relevant to Sri Lanka's digital policy and public sector modernization efforts.

items.title: Sri Lanka picked for first time in Four Seasons 2028 private jet tour
items.author: Ranul Seneviratne
items.summary: Sri Lanka has been selected for the first time as a stop on the Four Seasons Private Jet Experience for its 2028 around-the-world itinerary. Luxury travellers will spend three nights in the country, contributing to high-end tourism exposure.
